Subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Finovate (post-demo)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Great conversation — I wanted to capture the key takeaways and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap / stakeholders we heard today:
- Champion: Alex Johnson (you) — driving technical evaluation and internal pitch
- Economic buyer: Sarah Lee (CFO) — cares most about TCO and ROI
- Procurement: Kelly Park and procurement@finovate.com — will handle MSA/PO and security checklist
- Security lead: unknown yet, Alex mentioned they’ll loop in InfoSec if SOC 2 evidence is required

Decision criteria (as discussed):
1) Latency and predictable p99 under our expected load (15–30ms target for our primary flows)
2) Total cost of ownership and unit economics (token cost + infra)
3) Security/compliance (SOC 2, audit logs, VPC/private deployment options)
4) Ease of rollout / integration with current platform (Kafka + internal auth)

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll share a short mutual action plan (MAP) with owners and timelines — attached draft v1.
- Rishi to prepare a short technical one-pager and a tailored talk-track for Sarah (CFO) focusing on ROI.
- Schedule a procurement/contracting sync including Kelly + our commercial lead — can we target next week?

Can you confirm Sarah’s email and if procurement@finovate.com is the right procurement inbox? Also, any internal stakeholders we missed (InfoSec, Legal)?

I’ve attached: MAP-Finovate-v1.xlsx (draft) and Redwood-talk-tracks.pdf (internal enablement). I’ll follow up with calendar options.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — nice recap. A few quick clarifications so I can tailor the technical materials and the CFO talk-track: 

1) When Alex says "15–30ms target", is that for inline generation calls only or does it include batched async embedding/rerank workflows?
2) Do they have any strict throughput peaks (RPS) or token/sec targets we should size for?
3) For procurement / security, do we need to provide SOC 2 Type II + encryption-at-rest evidence up front or will that be handled later in the procurement funnel?

I'll draft a 1-page ROI summary that frames cost savings vs self-hosted + expected latency improvements and include a short technical appendix on routing/fallback options and our Dedicated/Private deployment tradeoffs. I can also put together a short email template Alex can share with Sarah.

If you want, I can join the procurement call to run through the SOC 2 docs and the tech appendix.

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes and the MAP. Quick answers: 

- Sarah Lee is the CFO (sarah.lee@finovate.com) — she is the primary economic buyer.
- procurement@finovate.com is the correct procurement inbox; Kelly Park (cc'ed) will own commercial/PO and contract routing.
- InfoSec: Stephen Ortiz (stephen.ortiz@finovate.com) will need SOC 2 evidence; he may ask for a short security questionnaire.
- Latency: primary concern is gen latency for our customer-facing flows (aim for p95 < 100ms and p99 as low as reasonably possible). Embedding batch jobs are less sensitive.
- Throughput: expected steady-state 60 reqs/sec for Q3 pilot with spiky peaks to ~250 reqs/sec for events.
- Timeline: internal review + procurement in ~3–6 weeks, hoping for contract signed by end of Q2.

I've attached the procurement form they asked us to fill out (Finovate-Procurement-Form.pdf) — Kelly, please confirm any additional docs you need from Redwood (e.g., invoice instructions, vendor setup).

Happy to set a 30-minute procurement sync next Tue or Wed.

Best,
